coordinates.locator: Table 5, "Coordinates estimates for various locations of interest", row "LUX Detector"
coordinates.note: Surface-projected position of the Davis Cavern detector hall, given by SURF for the LUX detector; LZ occupies the same cavern. Table 5 is headed "Coordinates estimates", so precision_m is set to 50 m rather than the arc-second resolution of the figures. The PDF text lists the table column by column: the first value in each column (599527, 4911873, 44 21 11.88 N, 103 45 04.27 W) belongs to the first row, LUX Detector; the other two rows are MJD Detector and Entrance Cutout. The rank-10 proceedings is the only source found that publishes coordinates; the official SURF Davis Campus page is co-cited for the location itself (A17).

name: Davis Campus, 4850 Level, Sanford Underground Research Facility
notes: The Davis Cavern is the excavation of Raymond Davis Jr.'s chlorine solar-neutrino experiment, begun in the mid-1960s; it was enlarged for dark matter experiments and the Davis Campus opened on 30 May 2012 (SURF, "The Davis Campus").
facility:surf is owned by the fermilab-dune workstream and is referenced, not created, here; this file will dangle until that file exists.
The Davis Campus hosted LUX (2013-2016) and now hosts LZ; the MAJORANA DEMONSTRATOR occupied the adjacent laboratory space.

summary.plain: A laboratory hall about 1.5 kilometres below the surface in a former gold mine in Lead, South Dakota. It was dug in the 1960s for Ray Davis's experiment that counted neutrinos from the Sun, and it now houses the LZ dark matter detector.
summary.technical: Davis Campus on the 4850 Level of SURF (former Homestake mine), ~1480 m of rock, ~4300 m.w.e. overburden. The enlarged Davis Cavern hosted LUX and now hosts LZ inside the 8 m × 6 m water shield; opened to science 30 May 2012.
